# Angular security

- Use interpolation and Angular bindings so values are escaped/sanitized for their context. Avoid direct DOM APIs and `ElementRef.nativeElement` writes with untrusted data.
- Do not call `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, `bypassSecurityTrustScript`, `bypassSecurityTrustStyle`, `bypassSecurityTrustUrl`, or `bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl` on untrusted or merely filtered values.
- Avoid runtime template compilation and dynamically constructed templates/components. Map external choices to a fixed component set and use AOT production builds.
- Treat route guards and hidden components as UX only. Enforce authentication, tenant, role, and object authorization in the backend.
- Keep Angular's XSRF integration aligned with the server cookie/header names and same-origin deployment. Do not disable it for cookie-authenticated state changes.
- Ensure authentication interceptors cover the intended API origins without sending tokens to third-party URLs. A browser token does not replace server authorization.
- Validate external URLs and use Angular's safe URL/resource mechanisms. Do not bind arbitrary schemes into `href`, `src`, iframe, or resource contexts.
- Keep secrets out of `environment*.ts`, build-time replacements, assets, and source maps; browser configuration is public.
- Use a strict CSP compatible with Angular and minimize third-party scripts. Do not add `unsafe-eval` to fix development-only behavior in production.
